subject: Architecture
title: Natural Ventilation: Wind as Air Conditioning
description: One-minute skill: Natural Ventilation: Wind as Air Conditioning.

hook.text: Before air conditioning, architects designed buildings that cooled themselves using wind and physics.

buildup.text: Cross-ventilation uses windows on opposite walls. Hot air rises and exits through high openings.

discovery.text: Persian wind catchers have cooled buildings for 3,000 years by funneling breezes down into rooms below.

twist.text: The Eastgate Centre in Zimbabwe mimics termite mounds — natural ventilation keeps it cool without AC.

climax.text: Air conditioning uses 10% of global electricity. Natural ventilation could slash that figure dramatically.

punchline.text: Termites solved cooling millions of years ago. We just forgot to ask them.
